scenes.title: Put Away That Chalk
scenes.summary: At eight Wednesday morning, F1 and M1 catch M2 drawing a crooked white chalk line down the 1890 mosaic floor with his glasses perched on his forehead.
scenes.intro: Eight sharp Wednesday morning inside the sunlit 1890 glass gallery! {F1} and {M1} walk in carrying buckets of warm soapy water—and freeze at the sight of {M2} on one knee holding a stick of white tailor chalk. Listen first.
story: F1
{M2}?! What on earth are you drawing down the middle of the mosaic tiles?!
M2
A polite, temporary white chalk line demarcating West Responsibility from East Responsibility!
M1
Stand up and look behind you, boss—your straight line curves like a river bend.
M2
Curves?! Impossible, I followed the blue mosaic diamonds with laser precision!
F1
Without pulling your reading glasses down from your forehead, {M2}—you followed a shadow!
M2
Oh dear... somehow West Responsibility just annexed that eastern porcelain glazing bench!
M1
Hand over the tailor chalk before you start a second sixty-year feud before coffee.
F1
Watch how one pass of {M1} and his damp mop restores peaceful diplomatic relations!
M2
Very well, zero chalk lines—how DO two houses share one room sensibly, {M1}?
M1
Same way two brothers share a saw: whoever uses it leaves it cleaner than before.
F1
Look up—{M3} just arrived on the upper balcony with the new skylight pane!
M1
Grab the Mop of Peace, boss, and start scrubbing the western cobalt skirting tiles.
scenes.outro: One sweep of a damp mop erases {M2}'s crooked border forever as skylight repair begins overhead! See you up top next time.

scenes.title: Bedding the Glass Pane
scenes.summary: Working safely from a padded plank between the brick parapets above the vault, M1 and M3 bed the new clear skylight pane in linseed putty while F2 hoists supplies.
scenes.intro: Up in the crisp morning air beside the second-floor parapet, {M1} and {M3} kneel on a wide bolted scaffold plank overlooking the conservatory ridge while {F2} sends up a canvas rope bucket. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
Bucket coming up on the pulley line: warm linseed glazier putty and brass clips!
M3
Got the handle safely, {F2}—not a single tool rattled against the glass!
M1
Old cracked pane lifted clean out of the iron T-bar; scrape the dry bed smooth.
M3
Notice how the eighteen-ninety ironworkers sloped tiny condensation channels inside every rib, {M1}!
M1
That is why zero rust ate this roof—smart drainage beats thick paint every decade.
F2
How does the new six-millimetre wired glass fit inside the old iron frame, gentlemen?
M3
Three millimetres of breathing room on all four edges, cushioned on rolled putty ribbons!
M1
Press firmly along the bevel with my glazing knife—smooth forty-five-degree waterproof seal.
F2
From down in the courtyard, the sun just flashed off that new pane like crystal!
M3
Pour one cup of test water across the ridge seam, {M1}, while {F2} checks below!
F2
Checking the mosaic floor inside right now... bone dry, zero drops anywhere!
M1
Sixty-year leak officially retired—now let us wash the other ninety-nine panes.
scenes.outro: Rolled linseed putty and nineteenth-century drainage channels seal the glass roof watertight once more! See you inside next time.

scenes.title: Vaulted Acoustic Sustain
scenes.summary: Testing musical pitch inside the newly sealed conservatory, F3 and M3 discover warm cathedral-like resonance—along with a lively wind tunnel whenever both outer doors stand open.
scenes.intro: At eleven Wednesday morning inside the sunlit vault, {F3} strikes a silver tuning fork and plays a soft phrase on a small reed pitch pipe while {M3} listens at the midpoint. Listen first.
story: F3
Listen to that A440 linger beneath the curved glass ceiling for three full seconds, {M3}!
M3
Curved tile vaults diffuse high frequencies evenly instead of slapping them straight back.
F3
A solo violin or flute in here will sound as warm as a wooden cello!
M3
Wait—feel what just happened when {M1} propped open our west courtyard door behind us!
F3
Goodness, did a brisk breeze just whistle straight through from the garden next door?!
M3
Two sun-warmed courtyards at slightly different temperatures create a classic pressure wind tunnel!
F3
If breezes rush through like that, music sheets will fly and bread loaves will cool!
M3
Hold on—look inside those two deep brick alcoves flanking the central arch rib!
F3
Are those folded wooden frames with bevelled leaded glass tucked flush against the brick?!
M3
Original eighteen-ninety interior wind-lobby doors, folded back on double-action brass hinges!
F3
So light and music pass right through clear glass while cross-winds stop completely!
M3
Let me fetch {M4} and his brass hinge pins—these doors want to swing again!
scenes.outro: Hidden inside brick alcoves for sixty years, bevelled leaded-glass wind doors solve the pressure breeze! See you next time.

scenes.title: Leaded Glass Wind-Doors
scenes.summary: On his noon break, M4 helps M3 free and balance the pair of 1890 leaded-glass wind doors while F1 polishes their bevelled diamond panes.
scenes.intro: At twelve-thirty inside the central arch of the glass passage, {M3} and {M4} ease two tall walnut-and-leaded-glass doors forward from their wall recesses as {F1} buffs the diamond panes with vinegar cloth. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M4
Careful on the bottom brass pivot, {M3}—one drop of clock oil and watch it swing!
M3
Whispers shut right at the centre stop without a latch, blocking every trace of draft!
F1
Look at the rainbows dancing across the cobalt wall tiles through these bevelled glass diamonds!
M4
Try walking through with a tea tray in both hands, {F1}—push gently with your elbow.
F1
Swings smoothly forward, then glides right back to centre behind me like a grand hotel!
M3
Whoever designed this conservatory in eighteen-ninety thought through airflow, heat, AND serving trays.
F1
Wait until you taste what {F2} is testing in the kitchen with those terracotta stamps!
M4
Did the four wheat-and-lyre medallions actually print cleanly onto risen bread dough?
F1
Come smell the café corner—she even invited {F3} to judge batch one!
M3
Once we wash the upper glass ribs today, ninety percent of our work is done.
M4
Leaving all of Thursday free to stage flowers before Friday and its noon photoshoot!
F1
Famous last words—let us eat warm bread before making promises about Thursday!
scenes.outro: Bevelled glass rainbows dance across cobalt brick while warm stamped bread beckons from the kitchen! See you next time.

scenes.title: Wheat and Lyre Bread Moulds
scenes.summary: In the café kitchen, F2 lifts golden round brioche-style honey loaves from the oven bearing crisp 1890 wheat-and-lyre medallions on their crusts.
scenes.intro: Inside the fragrant café kitchen, {F2} sets two round golden loaves onto a wooden board before {M4} and {F3}, each crown embossed with a crisp nineteenth-century medallion. Let us listen in first.
story: F3
Oh, {F2}, that wheat sheaf and musical lyre rose in the oven like sculpted bronze!
M4
How did you keep the risen dough from swallowing the fine carved lines while baking?
F2
Dusted the dry terracotta stamp lightly with rice flour and pressed right before glazing!
F3
And what gives the crust that deep amber shine without hiding the lyre strings?
F2
Saffron tea brushed with wildflower honey and a whisper of crushed roasted sesame!
M4
Tear off a warm piece from the test loaf, Chef—pure research for both courtyards!
F3
pillow-soft crumb, fragrant cardamom, and crisp sesame—our founders in eighteen-ninety ate royally!
F2
Even better: we wrapped one warm amphora-stamped loaf in linen for Number Twelve!
M4
Speaking of Number Twelve, she knocked on the glass wind-door five minutes ago with baskets!
F3
Baskets from next door?! What did our ceramic-restorer neighbour bring into the conservatory?!
F2
Wipe your crumbs, gentlemen and ladies—let us hurry out and meet her gift!
M4
Wait until {M2} sees what happens when you erase a chalk line!
scenes.outro: Rice-floured 1890 stamps turn golden honey loaves into edible art—just as baskets arrive from next door! See you in the conservatory next time.

scenes.title: Washing One Hundred Panes
scenes.summary: Using long bamboo extension sponges inside the conservatory, F1, M3, and F2 wash away decades of film until brilliant afternoon sun floods the cobalt tiles.
scenes.intro: At three Wednesday afternoon inside the vaulted gallery, {F1}, {M3}, and {F2} wield lightweight bamboo poles tipped with chamois squeegees along the curved glass ribs. Listen first.
story: F1
Pull your squeegee straight down rib seven, {M3}—watch sixty years of grey haze vanish!
F2
GOOD HEAVENS! Pure blue sky just poured onto the cobalt tiles like opening a curtain!
M3
Warm water with white vinegar cuts mineral film without leaving a single rainbow streak.
F1
Look at the glazed blue bricks along both walls—there are tiny gold stars fired inside!
F2
Nobody could see those gold lustre stars under dusty grey light yesterday afternoon!
M3
Only twelve lower panes left on the eastern curve, and every rib sparkles overhead.
F1
And look at the six hanging wire hooks along the iron tie-beams above the centre!
F2
Those are nineteenth-century fern hooks—the exact twin of the six ferns Number Twelve brought!
M3
Lush green fronds suspended overhead will filter harsh midday glare AND soften high echoes!
F1
Call {M2} in here to help hang the ferns and admire our handiwork!
F2
Look—here comes {M2} carrying a wooden tray wrapped in tissue paper from next door!
M3
Poles aside, everyone—what treasure just came out of that kiln next door?!
scenes.outro: Hidden gold lustre stars wake inside the cobalt bricks as sun pours through ninety-nine clean panes! See you next time.

scenes.title: Twelve Cobalt Cups Next Door
scenes.summary: Unwrapping a gift tray sent through the East Arch by Number Twelve, F2, F1, and M2 discover twelve hand-thrown cobalt-blue ceramic teacups matching the 1890 wall glaze.
scenes.intro: Setting a slatted potter's tray gently onto the conservatory bench, {M2} lifts away crisp white tissue paper before {F2} and {F1}. Listen first.
story: M2
Our neighbour thanked you for the amphora loaf, {F2}, and sent these in return!
F1
Gasp—twelve hand-thrown porcelain teacups glazed in the exact deep cobalt of these walls!
F2
Look at the tiny gold star fired inside the rim of every single saucer!
M2
She told me her grandfather mixed that cobalt-and-gold glaze formula in nineteen-twenty!
F1
And she kept twelve matching cups packed in tissue waiting for the conservatory to reopen!
F2
Twelve cobalt cups from Plot Fourteen-B plus twelve cream stoneware cups from Plot Fourteen-A!
M2
Alternating blue and cream all down one shared table—just like that nineteen-oh-five postcard!
F1
{M2}, I believe you have officially been cured of drawing white chalk lines!
M2
Chalk is for schoolrooms, {F1}; shared porcelain is for civilized historic neighbours!
F2
With all Thursday ahead of us, will Friday noon not feel wonderfully unhurried?!
F1
Wait—why is {M1} leaning out the lobby doorway holding up the telephone receiver?!
M2
Oh no, please do not tell me someone else caught an early train!
scenes.outro: Twelve heirloom cobalt cups seal a sixty-year reconciliation—right as the front-desk telephone strikes again! Final scene of Episode 4!

scenes.title: The Thursday Express Call
scenes.summary: At the front desk Wednesday evening, F1 takes a call from the National Guidebook Editor: storm clouds booked for Friday moved their photoshoot up to four sharp Thursday afternoon!
scenes.intro: Hurrying back to the front desk at six Wednesday evening, {F1} takes the black telephone receiver from {M1} while {M2} clutches his lapels. Listen first.
story: F1
Hello, {SHOW} speaking—yes, Chief Editor, how wonderful to hear from you!
M2
Whisper what she is saying, {F1}! Is Friday noon still confirmed?!
F1
Aha, heavy rain forecast across the region on Friday ruins natural skylight photography...
M1
Uh-oh—I know that tone of voice; clear Thursday afternoon light wins, right?
F1
Four sharp tomorrow afternoon works splendidly for us, Editor—safe travels, goodbye!
M2
FOUR SHARP THURSDAY AFTERNOON?! That is twenty-two hours from this exact minute!
M1
Relax, boss: the glass roof is sealed, washed, and shining, and the doors swing.
F1
All that remains tomorrow is hanging six ferns, testing the bread warmer, and baking!
M2
Plus polishing every tarnished brass pipe fitting inside that conservatory until it gleams!
M1
Whoa, hold everything—promise me right now you will NOT turn any unknown brass valves!
M2
Merely a soft dry polishing cloth, {M1}; what could possibly go wrong by four?!
F1
Set every alarm clock in {SHOW}—Thursday afternoon at four, history poses for its portrait!
scenes.outro: Friday clouds push the national photoshoot up to four sharp Thursday—and {M2} has his eye on an unknown brass valve! End of Episode 4—see you in Episode 5!
